introduction: North Dakota weatherization applications go through the Community Action agency serving your area. The agency evaluates the home and decides which improvements are appropriate.
description: North Dakota weatherization applications go through the Community Action agency serving your area. The agency evaluates the home and decides which improvements are appropriate

sections.who: Low-income owners and renters may qualify. The provider identifies LIHEAP recipients as income-eligible, but additional home and program requirements still apply.
sections.get: Approved work improves energy efficiency and household safety. Applicants are not charged a fee.
sections.docs:
• Household income or LIHEAP approval evidence.
  • Address and utility information.
  • Owner details and landlord consent information for a rental.
sections.apply:
1. Find the regional agency

    Use CAPND’s regional links to locate the provider.

  2. Request its application

    Ask for the current income checklist; the statewide page’s older dollar table should not replace current intake guidance.

  3. Arrange assessment

    Provide access and resolve required owner permissions before work can be scheduled.
sections.after: Keep the provider’s contact details and ask about waiting lists, assessment findings and any condition preventing work.
sections.sources: Checked October 1, 2026 using Housing types and regional intake, Eligibility and application guidance. USA Assistance background guide. Program staff determine eligibility and available assistance.

faqs: Yes, but the landlord must meet program requirements.
CAPND says manufactured homes, conventional houses and apartments can be served.
Does LIHEAP approval guarantee immediate work?
It can establish income eligibility; the provider still reviews other requirements and scheduling.

provenance.scope: Published eligibility, service purpose and application pathway; no unverified financial limits or deadlines included.
